title: Phorminx benchmarks

verdict.headline: Instant (Vosk) for live text, qwen2.5:7b for formatting

nudges.why: 4 engines got clear English speech about 0% wrong; pick by speed.
Instant is English-only; this got about 2% word errors.
qwen2.5:1.5b, gemma3:4b, qwen2.5:7b scored within 3 points of each other (about 96/100).
About 4.1 list lines per dictation in Structured and Custom, against 1.1 for the least list-happy model.
Feels instant (1.6 s), scores 95/100 and turns spoken lists into lists.
It changed about 6% of words and took 2.0× as long.
A one-minute meeting summarized in about 1 s.
Transcript saved about 0.1 s after Stop.
A full-HD screenshot reads in about 1.5 s with 0% character errors.
About 72 s to connect and add a contact over Tor, then about 0.8 s per message.
The window is ready about 1.3 s after launch.

summary:
A quick vibe check, not a lab test: one pass per setup on a typical desktop.

- **gemma3:4b did not fit in GPU memory** next to the other apps on the test desktop, so it decoded at about 2 tokens/s. Its times (and the timeouts behind its lower pass rate) show what happens when a model spills out of GPU memory, not how fast it is on a card where it fits. Its quality and list numbers still count.
- qwen2.5:1.5b was kept loaded by another app during the run, so its cold starts are often warm.
- The speech is synthetic and clean, so every recognizer looks near-perfect on accuracy; real voices and rooms are harder. Use these as nudges on speed.

features.title: Dictation
features.note: Generated speech (Windows voices Zira for English, Maria for Portuguese), 16 kHz mono. Live timings replay the recording at real time; Accurate's error rate is for the whole-recording text.

features.title: Formatting
features.note: 8 synthetic dictations (5 English, 3 Portuguese). Custom mode uses "Use short bullet points." Temperature 0.

features.title: Meetings
features.note: Generated two-voice meeting recordings (about a minute each) replayed at real time. Finalization is the last recognition tail plus saving the transcript. Summaries use the meeting assistant's request shape on the reference transcript.

features.title: Investigations
features.note: OCR runs on the CPU with the app's pinned PaddleOCR models on generated screenshots. Link previews fetch public pages over the internet, so they vary with the network. Answers use the investigation assistant's request shape.

features.title: Messaging
features.note: Two throwaway profiles on one machine. Loopback measures the messaging engine without a network; Tor uses the public Tor network, so its times vary with the circuits it builds.

features.title: App
features.note: A release build started on throwaway profiles with Instant dictation set up. Cold is the first start of a new profile; warm restarts it.

answer.label: Answer time
answer.description: From the request to the complete answer.

bootstrap.label: Tor bootstrap
bootstrap.description: From turning messaging on to being reachable.

cer.label: Character error rate
cer.description: Character edits needed to reach the text drawn on the screenshot, divided by its length.

coldStart.label: Cold start to first text
coldStart.description: Model load plus the first live text, in a process that had not loaded the model.

decodeRate.label: Decode speed
decodeRate.description: Tokens per second Ollama reported for a fixed 48-token prompt right after the run. Low values mean the model did not fit in GPU memory beside everything else on the card.

endToText.label: End of speech to text
endToText.description: From the end of the audio to the final text, replaying at real time.

fetch.label: Preview fetch
fetch.description: Fetching a page, its preview image and icon, and parsing the metadata.

finalize.label: Finalization
finalize.description: From Stop to a saved, final transcript.

firstMessage.label: First message
firstMessage.description: Send to delivered for the first message to a new contact.

firstText.label: Time to first live text
firstText.description: From the first spoken word to the first text on screen, replaying the audio at real time.

firstToken.label: Time to first token
firstToken.description: From the request to the first streamed word of the answer.

idleMemory.label: Memory at idle
idleMemory.description: Private memory 10 s after startup, the app plus the WebView2 processes it started.

latency.label: Latency
latency.description: Wall time from request to final text. Median of the repeats; p90 alongside.

laterPassChange.label: Second-pass change
laterPassChange.description: Share of words the second pass changed after the first.

listItems.label: List items
listItems.description: Mean number of list lines in the output.

loadTime.label: Model load
loadTime.description: Loading the recognition model into memory.

ocrTime.label: Recognition time
ocrTime.description: Detecting and reading every line of one screenshot.

parse.label: Metadata parse
parse.description: Parsing title, description and image from a saved page.

passRate.label: Validator pass rate
passRate.description: Share of runs whose output passed Phorminx's output validator and was inserted. A rejected output falls back to the text as spoken.

quality.label: Quality score
quality.description: 0-100. Kept facts (names, numbers, links: 50), filler words removed (20), sentence case and punctuation (15), lists where the mode asks for structure (15). Scored on the text Phorminx would insert.

redeem.label: Invite redeem
redeem.description: From pasting an invite to both sides seeing the contact.

rtf.label: Real-time factor
rtf.description: Compute time divided by audio length. Below 1 keeps up with speech.

rtt.label: Message round trip
rtt.description: Send to delivered for later messages on an open connection.

startup.label: Startup to window
startup.description: From launch to the main window being ready.

wer.label: Word error rate
wer.description: Word edits needed to reach the reference text, divided by its length; case and punctuation ignored.

examples.input: Should we switch to Northwind Cloud? What would block it?
examples.output:
Based on the available information, the decision to switch hosting with Northwind Cloud seems to hinge on three main factors:

1. **Security and Data Safety**: The screenshot from the Quarterly operations report shows a significant increase in uptime to 99.71%, with only two incidents over an hour, compared to the current uptime of 99.95%. However, the question also asks about what would block it, indicating there might be concerns about security or data safety despite the higher uptime. The current provider has two incidents longer than an hour, which is a concern.

2. **Cost**: There's a cost difference between the current provider at $41,000 per year and Northwind Cloud at $45,000 per year. The finance team can approve up to $45,000 per year without a board vote, indicating that the budget is there, but the question asks about potential barriers beyond cost. It’s possible that additional security measures or compliance requirements might be required that exceed the $45,000 budget.

3. **Contract Terms**: The finance team prefers contracts of two years or less, and they are more willing to approve contracts of two years or less than those of longer durations. A contract with Northwind Cloud of three years would not be approved, so this aspect is a potential barrier as well.

In summary, the security and data safety aspect appears to be the primary concern, as even with higher uptime compared to the current provider, the security issues might make it a concern for the finance team. The cost, while not a direct barrier, could be a concern if additional security measures or compliance requirements exceed the $45,000 budget. The contract duration is a clear barrier, as a three-year contract would not be approved, regardless of the increased uptime.
